newsitem.title: USA: ComEd Illinois nuke to reduce power output.
newsitem.headline: ComEd Illinois nuke to reduce power output.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co's (ComEd) 794 megawatt Dresden nuclear power unit 3 will reduce electricity output over the next several months as the last of the unit's fuel is spent, a company spokesman said.
"The fuel in the reactor is reaching the end of its cycle. We will continue to coast down to where we can't get anymore power out of that fuel," spokesman Art Massa said Friday.
The Morris, Ill. unit is expected to operate as long as it can at reducing levels as the last of the fuel is spent.
The coastdown is expected to take several months. No date has yet been set to shut the unit for refueling, Massa said.
Dresden 3 was operating at near 85 percent of capacity as of Friday, he said.

Typically, nuclear operating companies will set a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage once every 18 months for each nuclear unit and will sometimes coast power levels down just ahead of the shutdown.
But Massa said it was not unusual for ComEd to squeeze as much operating capability out of a unit as it can before the fuel supply ends and the shutdown becomes necessary.
"We do this often. Our intent is to get as much use out of that fuel as we can."
ComEd is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
